title: Greatest Common Divisor of Strings
summary: Find the longest nonempty string whose repeated copies form both input strings exactly.

contractDetails.constraints: Each string has 1–1000 uppercase English letters.
contractDetails.output-checking: Exact typed equality of the returned str.

statement: Find the longest nonempty string whose repeated copies form both input strings exactly. Return an empty string if there is no common repeated base.

examples.explanation: The two strings use three and two copies of XY.
The longer common base uses two Ms.
No prefix tiles both strings completely.

constraints: Each string has 1–1000 uppercase English letters.
hints: Conceptual: A common base must divide both lengths.
Directional: A shared repetition pattern makes the two concatenation orders equal.
Implementation: Check that concatenating the strings in either order gives the same result. If so, take a prefix whose length is the greatest common divisor of the two lengths.
complexityAnalysis: O(a+b) time and O(a+b) temporary space when materializing the concatenations. Comparing their characters directly uses O(1) extra state.
